topics.name: Reciprocity
topics.desc: Giving first so the other person feels they owe something back.
topics.q: The rule that we feel obliged to repay what others give us: gifts, favours and free samples create a sense of debt and indebtedness that makes people comply.

topics.name: Reciprocal concessions
topics.desc: Ask big, then retreat to a smaller request that now feels like a concession.
topics.q: Making a large request that will be refused, then retreating to a smaller one; the retreat feels like a concession the other person must answer with a concession of their own.

topics.name: Commitment & consistency
topics.desc: Once people take a stand, they act to stay consistent with it.
topics.q: Once people make a commitment or take a stand, especially publicly or in writing, they feel pressure to behave consistently with it, even when it no longer serves them.

topics.name: Social proof
topics.desc: Deciding what is right by watching what others do, especially when unsure.
topics.q: People decide what is correct by watching what others like them are doing, especially under uncertainty; crowds, bystanders and imitation drive behaviour.

topics.name: Liking
topics.desc: We say yes to people we like: the similar, the attractive, the flattering.
topics.q: We comply with people we like; liking grows from physical attractiveness, similarity, compliments, familiarity, cooperation and association with good things.

topics.name: Authority
topics.desc: Deference to titles, uniforms and experts, even when it makes no sense.
topics.q: Obedience and deference to authority figures, experts, titles, uniforms and symbols of status, even when following them is harmful or absurd.

topics.name: Scarcity
topics.desc: Things seem more valuable when they are rare, limited, or being taken away.
topics.q: Opportunities seem more valuable when they are scarce, limited or being lost; deadlines, limited numbers and forbidden things increase desire.

topics.name: Mental shortcuts
topics.desc: Automatic click-whirr responses that skip thinking.
topics.q: Automatic, fixed-action patterns and mental shortcuts: people respond to a single trigger feature without thinking the decision through, which others can exploit.

topics.name: Reputation
topics.desc: Your name is your power: guard it, and undermine your rival's.
topics.q: Reputation as the cornerstone of power: building a strong name, guarding it with your life, and attacking or destroying the reputation of rivals.

topics.name: Attention & spectacle
topics.desc: Being seen, at any cost, through drama and striking images.
topics.q: Courting attention at all costs, standing out from the crowd through spectacle, scandal, striking images and theatrical displays that make you larger than life.

topics.name: Hidden intentions
topics.desc: Keeping your real goal out of sight with decoys and smoke screens.
topics.q: Concealing your true intentions and goals behind decoys, false sincerity and smoke screens so others cannot prepare a defence.

topics.name: Saying less
topics.desc: The less you say, the more powerful and mysterious you appear.
topics.q: Saying less than necessary: silence and brevity make you seem powerful and mysterious, while talking too much reveals weakness and gets you into trouble.

topics.name: Absence & withdrawal
topics.desc: Pulling away to make your presence more valued.
topics.q: Using absence and strategic withdrawal to increase respect and longing; too much presence cheapens you, while pulling away makes others value and pursue you.

topics.name: Suspense & unpredictability
topics.desc: Keeping others guessing so they stay off balance and engaged.
topics.q: Cultivating unpredictability and suspense, mixing hot and cold and surprising people, so they stay off balance, anxious and absorbed in you.

topics.name: Dependence
topics.desc: Making yourself needed so others cannot do without you.
topics.q: Making others dependent on you so you become indispensable; the more people need you, the more freedom and power you have.

topics.name: Isolation
topics.desc: Cutting people off, or being cut off yourself, and why it is dangerous.
topics.q: Isolation: separating a target from friends and family to increase control over them, and the danger of cutting yourself off from others.

topics.name: Appealing to self-interest
topics.desc: People help when they see what is in it for them, not out of gratitude.
topics.q: When asking for help, appeal to people's self-interest rather than their mercy or gratitude; show what they will gain.

topics.name: Enemies & rivals
topics.desc: Using enemies, crushing them completely, or refusing to notice them.
topics.q: Dealing with enemies and rivals: distrusting friends, making use of enemies, crushing an opponent totally, or disdaining what you cannot have.

topics.name: Timing & patience
topics.desc: Waiting for the right moment, and planning all the way to the end.
topics.q: Mastering timing and patience: waiting for the right moment, never appearing hurried, and planning all the way to the end before acting.

topics.name: Boldness
topics.desc: Acting with audacity; hesitation and timidity give you away.
topics.q: Entering action with boldness and audacity; hesitation, timidity and half-measures reveal weakness and invite failure.

topics.name: Fantasy & illusion
topics.desc: Feeding people's dreams instead of their reality.
topics.q: Playing to people's fantasies and illusions: offering a dream or escape from dull reality rather than the truth, so they follow you.

topics.name: Mirroring
topics.desc: Reflecting someone's moods and values back to disarm or captivate them.
topics.q: Mirroring another person's moods, tastes, values and spirit so they feel understood and lower their guard; becoming a reflection of their desires.

topics.name: Strategic weakness
topics.desc: Surrender, vulnerability and imperfection used as a source of power.
topics.q: Using weakness, surrender, vulnerability or imperfection strategically to disarm others and gain power.

topics.name: Charm
topics.desc: Making people feel good about themselves so they lower their guard.
topics.q: The art of charm: focusing attention on the other person, making them feel good about themselves and comfortable, so they become pliable.

topics.name: Charisma & presence
topics.desc: The magnetic quality that makes people want to follow you.
topics.q: Charisma and presence: confidence, purpose, energy and mystery that make people magnetically drawn to follow a person.

topics.name: Desire & temptation
topics.desc: Stirring want by showing what someone lacks and dangling it close.
topics.q: Creating desire and temptation: stirring a sense of lack and longing, dangling something forbidden or just out of reach.

topics.name: Insinuation & words
topics.desc: Planting ideas indirectly so people think they thought of them.
topics.q: Insinuation and seductive language: planting ideas indirectly through hints, ambiguous words and suggestion so people believe the ideas are their own.

topics.name: Indirect approach
topics.desc: Lowering defences with honesty, generosity or a friendly approach first.
topics.q: Approaching indirectly: disarming a target with selective honesty, generosity or friendship before revealing your aims.

topics.name: Jealousy & triangles
topics.desc: Using rivals and envy to raise your value.
topics.q: Stirring jealousy and creating triangles: showing that others desire you to increase your value and make someone compete for you.

topics.name: Belief & cults
topics.desc: People's need to believe, and how followings and faith are created.
topics.q: People's overwhelming need to believe in something; how cult-like followings, faith and devotion are created around a leader or cause.

topics.name: Controlling the options
topics.desc: Letting people choose, but only between options that all favour you.
topics.q: Controlling the options: giving people the feeling of free choice while every option offered works in your favour.

topics.name: Dealing with superiors
topics.desc: Never outshining the master; playing the perfect courtier.
topics.q: Dealing with superiors and masters: never outshining them, flattering them subtly, and playing the perfect courtier.

topics.name: Reactance
topics.desc: Push people and they push back to defend their freedom.
topics.q: Psychological reactance: when people feel their freedom of choice is threatened or restricted, they resist, want the forbidden thing more and do the opposite of what they are told.

topics.name: Bystander effect
topics.desc: In a crowd, everyone waits for someone else to help.
topics.q: The bystander effect and pluralistic ignorance: in emergencies people in a group fail to help because responsibility is diffused and each looks to the others' calm to decide nothing is wrong.

topics.name: Cooperation builds liking
topics.desc: Working toward a shared goal turns rivals into friends.
topics.q: Cooperation toward shared goals builds liking and reduces hostility: joint tasks, common enemies and interdependence, as in the jigsaw classroom and summer camp experiments.

topics.name: Cons & greed
topics.desc: Swindlers hook their marks through greed and hope.
topics.q: Con artists and swindles: how frauds exploit greed, vanity and the desire for easy money, dangling a prize to make the mark trust and hand over money.

topics.name: Knowing when to stop
topics.desc: Victory breeds arrogance; quit while you are ahead.
topics.q: Hubris and overreaching: success makes people arrogant and reckless; knowing when to stop, not going past the mark you aimed for, and consolidating gains instead of pushing luck.

topics.name: Seducer types
topics.desc: The Rake, the Siren, the Coquette and other seductive characters.
topics.q: Types of seducers and their seductive character: the Siren, the Rake, the Ideal Lover, the Dandy, the Natural, the Coquette, the Charmer, the Charismatic and the Star, and the anti-seducer.

topics.name: Sensual lures
topics.desc: Lowering defences through the senses and the body.
topics.q: Physical and sensual lures in seduction: appealing to the senses with pleasure, clothing, scent, touch, sights and spectacle, mixing the spiritual with the sensual to stir physical desire.

topics.name: Dark triad
topics.desc: Narcissism, Machiavellianism and psychopathy.
topics.q: The dark triad personality traits: narcissism, Machiavellianism and psychopathy; manipulators who lack empathy and remorse, exploit others, crave admiration and use people as tools.

topics.name: Narcissistic abuse
topics.desc: Idealise, devalue, discard: the narcissist's cycle.
topics.q: Narcissists and narcissistic abuse in relationships: grandiosity, need for admiration, idealise-devalue-discard cycle, entitlement, rage at criticism and draining the partner.

topics.name: Gaslighting
topics.desc: Making someone doubt their own memory and sanity.
topics.q: Gaslighting: denying what happened, rewriting events and insisting the victim is wrong, forgetful or crazy until they doubt their own memory, perception and judgment.

topics.name: Love bombing
topics.desc: Flooding a target with affection to hook them fast.
topics.q: Love bombing: overwhelming a new target with excessive attention, flattery, gifts and declarations of love to create fast attachment and dependence before control begins.

topics.name: Guilt & emotional blackmail
topics.desc: Fear, obligation and guilt used as levers.
topics.q: Emotional blackmail and guilt-tripping: using fear, obligation and guilt, threats, sulking and playing the victim to make someone give in to demands.

topics.name: Emotional manipulation
topics.desc: Steering behaviour by playing on feelings.
topics.q: Emotional manipulation: exploiting another person's emotions, insecurities and empathy to control their behaviour, through fear, flattery, shame, pity and mood swings.

topics.name: Mind games
topics.desc: Silent treatment, projection, moving goalposts.
topics.q: Manipulative mind games and tactics: the silent treatment, projection, triangulation, moving the goalposts, playing dumb, minimising, lying by omission and putting the target on the defensive.

topics.name: Covert NLP
topics.desc: Pacing, leading, anchors and embedded commands.
topics.q: Neuro-linguistic programming used to influence covertly: pacing and leading, anchoring a feeling to a touch or word, embedded commands, presuppositions and hypnotic language patterns.

topics.name: Mind control & brainwashing
topics.desc: Breaking down identity and rebuilding belief.
topics.q: Mind control and brainwashing: isolating people, breaking down their identity, controlling information, repetition, sleep deprivation and rewards and punishments to reshape beliefs.

topics.name: Dark persuasion
topics.desc: Persuading people against their own interest.
topics.q: Dark persuasion: persuading people to act against their own interests or values, using deceit, pressure and hidden motives, compared with positive, ethical persuasion.

topics.name: Lies & deception tactics
topics.desc: How manipulators lie, half-truth and mislead.
topics.q: Deception as a manipulation tactic: lying, half-truths, exaggeration, implication, strategic omission and creating false impressions to mislead the target.

topics.name: Who gets targeted
topics.desc: Traits that make someone easy to manipulate.
topics.q: Victims of manipulation: who manipulators target, such as people who are lonely, insecure, naive, people-pleasing, emotionally dependent or highly empathic, and why.

topics.name: Spotting a manipulator
topics.desc: Warning signs you are being manipulated.
topics.q: Signs you are being manipulated: red flags of a manipulative or toxic person, feeling confused, guilty or drained, inconsistencies and pressure, and how to recognise covert control.

topics.name: Defending yourself
topics.desc: Boundaries and counters against manipulation.
topics.q: Protecting yourself from manipulation and dark psychology: setting boundaries, saying no, staying calm, refusing to engage, cutting contact and regaining self-esteem.

topics.name: Body language basics
topics.desc: Reading clusters, context and congruence.
topics.q: Reading body language: nonverbal signals, gesture clusters, context and congruence between words and body, and why most communication is nonverbal.

topics.name: Hands, arms & posture
topics.desc: Palms, crossed arms and open versus closed posture.
topics.q: Hand and arm gestures and posture: palm signals, crossed arms as barriers, steepling, hand-to-face gestures, leg crossing and open or closed body positions.

topics.name: Eye signals
topics.desc: Gaze, pupils and what eyes give away.
topics.q: Eye signals: gaze patterns, eye contact, dilated pupils, looking away, eye blocking and blinking, and how eyes reveal interest, attraction and dominance.

topics.name: Dominance & status signals
topics.desc: How power shows in the body.
topics.q: Nonverbal dominance and status signals: handshakes, taking up space, territory, height, posture and positioning that show power, confidence or submission.

topics.name: Courtship signals
topics.desc: How attraction shows in the body.
topics.q: Courtship and flirting body language: signals of romantic interest and attraction shown by men and women, preening, glances, touching and leaning in.

topics.name: Faces & micro-expressions
topics.desc: Universal expressions and fleeting leaks.
topics.q: Facial expressions of emotion: universal expressions across cultures, micro-expressions and subtle expressions that briefly leak concealed feelings on the face.

topics.name: What triggers emotions
topics.desc: Why we feel what we feel, and when.
topics.q: Emotion triggers and the emotional alert database: what sets off emotions automatically, the refractory period, and how we can change what we become emotional about.

topics.name: Signs of a lie
topics.desc: Verbal and nonverbal deception indicators.
topics.q: Detecting deception: verbal and nonverbal indicators of lying, failing to answer, non-denials, attack mode, qualifiers, timing of behaviour and clusters of deceptive signs.

topics.name: Getting the truth
topics.desc: Questions and methods that draw out the truth.
topics.q: Eliciting the truth: questioning techniques, open questions, bait questions, the deception-detection model, interviewing and getting a liar to confess.

topics.name: Two systems
topics.desc: Fast intuition versus slow, lazy reasoning.
topics.q: System 1 and System 2: fast automatic intuitive thinking versus slow effortful deliberate reasoning; the lazy controller, cognitive ease and mental effort.

topics.name: Anchoring
topics.desc: The first number sets the frame.
topics.q: The anchoring effect: an initial number or reference point, even an arbitrary one, biases later estimates, judgments, prices and negotiations.

topics.name: Availability & vividness
topics.desc: What comes to mind easily feels likely.
topics.q: The availability heuristic: judging frequency and risk by how easily examples come to mind; vivid, recent and emotional events distort our estimates.

topics.name: Framing & loss aversion
topics.desc: Losses loom larger than gains.
topics.q: Framing effects and loss aversion: the same choice described as a gain or a loss changes decisions; losses hurt about twice as much as equal gains; prospect theory.

topics.name: Overconfidence
topics.desc: We know less than we think we do.
topics.q: Overconfidence and the illusion of understanding: hindsight bias, the illusion of validity, expert intuition, the planning fallacy and narrative fallacy.

topics.name: Cognitive dissonance
topics.desc: Justifying what we did to feel consistent.
topics.q: Cognitive dissonance and self-justification: people change attitudes to justify their behaviour and decisions, rationalise effort and suffering, and defend their self-image.

topics.name: Conformity & obedience
topics.desc: Bending to the group and to orders.
topics.q: Conformity and obedience: the Asch line experiments and Milgram obedience studies; why people go along with groups and follow orders against their judgment.

topics.name: Prejudice & stereotypes
topics.desc: How we prejudge groups and why.
topics.q: Prejudice, stereotypes and discrimination: in-groups and out-groups, scapegoating, and how prejudice forms and can be reduced.
